title: Ten Arguments For Deleting Your Social Media Accounts Right Now

questions.q: According to Lanier, how do social media platforms treat their users?
a: As the product, whose data is sold to advertisers
As guests, whose privacy is carefully protected
As customers, who pay a small monthly fee
As partners, who share in the platform’s profits
questions.why: Lesson 1 says every bit of information you share is sold, making you the product rather than the customer.

questions.q: Why does unpredictable feedback keep people coming back to social apps?
a: Unreliable rewards are more engaging than reliable ones
It makes the platform feel more honest and human
It teaches users to recognize and skip the ads
It rewards people for logging off and taking breaks
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that behaviorists found moderate unreliability more engaging, and algorithms exploit that.

questions.q: What does Lanier say is the real problem he wants to fix?
a: The manipulative business model, not the technology itself
The amount of time people waste on their phones
The slow speed of internet connections worldwide
The shortage of worthwhile content on the platforms
questions.why: Lesson 2 stresses that you need not throw out your smartphone, only stop feeding the model he names.

questions.q: Which two US companies rely solely on the business model Lanier criticizes?
a: Facebook and Google
Apple and Microsoft
Amazon and Twitter
Netflix and Spotify
questions.why: Lesson 2 notes that only these two US firms depend entirely on that model, while others use parts of it.

questions.q: What happens to people when they shift into what Lanier calls pack mode?
a: They focus on status and treat others more harshly
They become more creative and more cautious
They seek privacy and avoid group settings
They listen more carefully to opposing views
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts cautious, kind solitary mode with pack mode, where social rank trumps everything.
